He made provision (mut'ah) for the first, and for the second He made half the bridal gift (sadaq) due, on account of the harm to the wife from the nullifying of the contract and the stain upon the lawfulness that the husband obtained through the contract; and He set the dower that is due against the touching.

The third: When Allah, exalted is He, divided the condition of the divorced woman here into two categories, one for whom a named dower is stipulated and one for whom none was named, this indicates that the marriage of delegation (nikah al-tafwid) is permissible. This is every marriage contracted without mention of the bridal gift, and there is no disagreement about it. Afterward the bridal gift is fixed; if it is fixed, it joins the contract and is valid. If no dower was fixed for her and the divorce occurred, no dower is due, by consensus, as stated by al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi. Al-Mahdawi related from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman that if he divorced her without consummation and no dower had been fixed for her, he is compelled to pay half the dower of her equivalent. If a dower is fixed after the contract of marriage and before the divorce occurs, Abu Hanifa said: it is not halved by the divorce, because it was not due by the contract. This contradicts the apparent meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already fixed for them a dower﴾, and it also contradicts analogy, for a dower fixed after the contract joins the contract, so it must be halved by divorce, its root being the dower fixed together with the contract.

The fourth: If death occurs before a dower is fixed. al-Tirmidhi related from Ibn Mas'ud that he was asked about a man who married a woman, did not fix a dower for her, did not consummate with her, and then died. Ibn Mas'ud said: she has the like of the dower of her women, neither less nor excessive, and she must observe the waiting period, and she has inheritance. Ma'qil ibn Sinan al-Ashja'i stood up and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) decided in the case of Bir'a bint Washiq, a woman from among us, the same as what you have decided. Ibn Mas'ud rejoiced at this. Al-Tirmidhi said: The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud is a hasan sahih hadith, and it has been related from him through more than one route; and it is acted upon by some of the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and others, and al-Thawri, Ahmad and Ishaq hold this view. Some people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), including 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, said: If a man marries a woman, does not consummate with her, and does not fix a dower for her until he dies, they said: she has inheritance, and she has no dower, and she must observe the waiting period. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, who said: Even if the hadith of Bir'a bint Washiq were established, the proof would lie in what is related from the Prophet (ﷺ). It is related from al-Shafi'i that he later retracted this view in Egypt and adopted the hadith of Bir'a bint Washiq.

I say: There has been disagreement over the authenticity of the hadith of Bir'a. Al-Qadi Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Wahhab, in his commentary on the Risala of Ibn Abi Zayd, said: As for the hadith of Bir'a bint Washiq, the hadith memorizers and the imams of the people of knowledge have rejected it. Al-Waqidi said: This report occurred in Medina and no scholar accepted it. Al-Tirmidhi authenticated it, as we have related from him, and so did Ibn al-Mundhir. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The like of the statement of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and by it we say. It is mentioned that this is also the view of Abu Thawr and the people of opinion.

It is related from al-Zuhri, al-Awza'i, Malik and al-Shafi'i the like of the view of 'Ali, Zayd, Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar. There is a third view on the issue: that there is no inheritance unless there is a dower, said by Masruq. I say: Among the proofs for what Malik held is that it is a separation in a marriage before a dower is fixed, so no bridal gift is due in it, its root being divorce. But if the hadith is authentic, then analogy against it is invalid. Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Hamid has related from the school what agrees with the hadith, and praise be to Allah. Abu 'Umar said: The hadith of Bir'a was related by 'Abd al-Razzaq from al-Thawri from Mansur from Ibrahim from 'Alqama from Ibn Mas'ud, the hadith... In it: Ma'qil ibn Sinan stood up. Ibn Mahdi related it from al-Thawri from Firas from al-Sha'bi from Masruq from 'Abd Allah, and said: Ma'qil ibn Yasar. In my view the correct version is that of the one who said Ma'qil ibn Sinan, not Ma'qil ibn Yasar, because Ma'qil ibn Yasar was a man from Muzayna, while this hadith came concerning a woman from Ashja', not from Muzayna. Likewise Dawud related it from al-Sha'bi from 'Alqama, and in it: some men from Ashja' said. Ma'qil ibn Sinan was killed on the day of al-Harra, and on the day of al-Harra the poet says:

Behold, those are the Ansar weeping for their chiefs,
and Ashja' weeps for Ma'qil ibn Sinan.

The fifth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿as long as you have not touched them﴾. "Ma" here means "alladhi" (those whom), i.e. if you divorce the women whom you have not touched. And "tamassuhunna" has been read with a fatha on the ta' from the triliteral form, which is the reading of Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, 'Asim and Ibn 'Amir. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "tamasuhunna" from the form of mufa'ala, because the intercourse is completed by both of them; and the form fa'ala may come in the pattern of mufa'ala with the meaning of fa'ala, such as "tarraqtu al-na'l" (I mended the sandal) and "'aqabtu al-liss" (I punished the thief). The first reading implies the meaning of mufa'ala in this pattern with the sense understood from the touch, and Abu 'Ali preferred it, because verbs of this meaning came in the triliteral on this measure: nakaha, safada, qara'a, dafata, and "darab al-fahl" (the stallion mounted). Both readings are good. As for "aw" in "aw tafridu" (or you fix), it is said to have the meaning of "wa" (and), i.e. as long as you have not touched them and have not fixed for them a dower, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a city have We destroyed, so Our punishment came upon it by night or while they were at noon [qa'ilun]﴾ (see vol. 7, p. 162), meaning "wa-hum qa'ilun" (and they were at noon). And His saying: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ (see vol. 15, p. 130), meaning "wa-yazidun" (and they increase). And His saying: ﴿Do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾ (see vol. 19, p. 146), meaning "wa-kafuran" (and a disbeliever). And His saying: ﴿And if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself﴾ (see vol. 6, p. 199), meaning "wa-ja'a ahadun minkum mina al-ghaait" (and one of you came from the place of relieving himself) while you are ill or travelling. And His saying: ﴿except what their backs have carried or the entrails or what is mixed with bone﴾ (see vol. 7, p. 124), and the like of it. This is supported by the fact that He, exalted is He, afterward joined to it the woman who has been fixed a dower, saying: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already fixed for them a dower﴾. For if the first were explaining the divorce of the one for whom a dower was fixed before touching, He would not have repeated it.

The sixth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and provide for them﴾. Its meaning is: give them something that will be a provision for them. Ibn 'Umar, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Qilaba, al-Zuhri, Qatada and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim interpreted it as obligatory. Abu 'Ubayd, Malik ibn Anas and his companions, the judge Shurayh and others interpreted it as recommended. The first group held to the requirement of the command. The second group held to His saying, exalted is He: "a duty upon the doers of good" and "upon the God-fearing"; and had it been obligatory, He would have made it binding upon all creation. The first view is more correct, because the general forms of the command to provide in His saying "provide for them," and the attribution of the provision to them by the particle of ownership in His saying "and for the divorced women is a provision," are more apparent in obligation than in recommendation. His saying "upon the God-fearing" is an emphasis on its obligation, because every person is obliged to fear Allah regarding associating others with Him and His disobedience. Allah, exalted is He, has said in the Qur'an: ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ (see vol. 1, p. 161).

The seventh: They differed concerning the pronoun attached to His saying "and provide for them": to which of the women does it refer? Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Jabir ibn Zayd, al-Hasan, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, 'Ata', Ishaq and the people of opinion said: provision is obligatory for the divorced woman before consummation and before a dower is fixed, and recommended for the others. Malik and his companions said: provision is recommended for every divorced woman, even if she has been consummated with, except the one who has not been consummated with and for whom a dower has been fixed; for her, what was fixed for her suffices, and she has no provision. Abu Thawr said: she has provision, and so does every divorced woman. The scholars agreed that the one for whom no dower was fixed and who has not been consummated with is owed nothing except provision. al-Zuhri said: the judge decides it for her. The majority of people said: the judge does not decide it for her.

I say: this consensus applies only to the free woman (ḥurrah). As for a slave-woman (amah) who is divorced before the fixing of the dower (fard) and before consummation (masis), the majority hold that she is entitled to a provision (mut'ah). Al-Awza'i and al-Thawri said: she has no mut'ah, because it goes to her master, and he does not deserve property in exchange for the distress his slave suffers through divorce.

As for the position of the school of Malik, Ibn Sha'ban said: the mut'ah is in return for the grief of divorce, and therefore a woman who obtains khul' (khul'ah), a woman who obtains mubara'ah, and a woman divorced by li'an (mula'anah) has no mut'ah, either before or after consummation, because she is the one who chose the divorce. At-Tirmidhi, 'Ata' and al-Nakha'i said: the woman who obtains khul' has a mut'ah. The people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) said: the woman divorced by li'an has a mut'ah.

Ibn al-Qasim said: there is no mut'ah in a marriage that has been annulled (mafsukh). Ibn al-Mawwaz said: nor in anything in which annulment occurs after the validity of the contract, such as one spouse coming to own the other. Ibn al-Qasim said: the basis of this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for divorced women there is a provision according to what is reasonable﴾, so this ruling is specific to divorce and not to annulment.

Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that a woman given the choice (al-mukhayyarah) has a mut'ah, unlike a slave-woman who is freed under a slave husband and then chooses for herself; for her there is no mut'ah. As for a free woman who is given the choice, or made to own (tumlak), or whose husband marries a slave-woman over her, and she then chooses for herself in all of these cases, she has a mut'ah, because the husband is the cause of the separation.

The eighth issue: Malik said: there is no known limit for the mut'ah among us, neither for its minimum nor its maximum. People have differed on this. Ibn 'Umar said: the least that suffices as mut'ah is thirty dirhams or its equivalent. Ibn 'Abbas said: the highest form of mut'ah is a servant, then clothing, then maintenance. 'Ata': the middle of it is a shirt (dir'), a head-covering (khimar) and a wrap (milhafah). Abu Hanifa: that is its minimum. Ibn Muhayriz said: upon the holder of the register (diwan) three dinars, and upon the slave, mut'ah. Al-Hasan said: each person gives mut'ah according to his means: this one with a servant, this one with garments, this one with a garment, this one with maintenance. Malik ibn Anas says likewise, and this is what the Qur'an requires, for Allah, glorified is He, did not specify or limit it, but said: "upon the wealthy is his measure, and upon the straitened is his measure." Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali gave mut'ah of twenty thousand (dirhams), a jar of honey (ziqaq) and honey. Shurayh gave mut'ah of five hundred dirhams.

It has also been said that the woman's condition is likewise to be considered. This was said by some of the Shafi'is, who said: if we considered only the man's condition, it would follow that if he married two women, one of noble standing and the other of low standing, and then divorced them both before consummation without having specified a dower for them, they would be equal in mut'ah, so that the low-standing woman would be owed what the noble one is owed. This contradicts what Allah, exalted is He, said: "a provision according to what is reasonable." It would also follow that a man of great wealth who marries a woman of low standing would give her the same as a man of modest means, because if he divorces her before consummation and before fixing the dower, mut'ah becomes due upon him according to his means and her equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl). The mut'ah would then be many times her equivalent dower, so she would have become entitled before consummation to many times what she would be entitled to after consummation from the equivalent dower, which is the extreme of humiliation, namely intercourse.

The people of opinion and others said: the mut'ah of a woman divorced before consummation and before fixing the dower is only half of her equivalent dower, no more, because the equivalent dower is due by the contract, and mut'ah is a part of the equivalent dower. So it is owed to her just as half of the stipulated dower is owed when he divorces before consummation. This is refuted by His saying: ﴿upon the wealthy is his measure, and upon the straitened is his measure﴾, and this is evidence for rejecting fixed limitation. And Allah is All-Knowing of the realities of matters.

Al-Tha'labi mentioned a hadith: He said: the verse "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women..." was revealed concerning a man of the Ansar who married a woman of Banu Hanifa and did not specify a dower for her, then divorced her before touching her, and the verse was revealed. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Give her mut'ah, even if it be with your cap."

Al-Daraqutni narrated from Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, who said: 'A'ishah al-Khath'amiyyah was married to al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. When 'Ali was struck and al-Hasan was given the oath of allegiance to the caliphate, she said: "May the caliphate bring you joy, O Commander of the Believers." He said: "'Ali is killed and you show gloating! Go, for you are divorced three times." He said: she wrapped herself in her sajj [[In manuscripts J and H: "bi-jalabibiha" (in her outer garment). The sajj is a large, thick tayalisan. It was also said it is a patterned tayalisan woven in that manner.]] and sat until her waiting period (iddah) ended. Then he sent to her ten thousand as mut'ah, and the remainder of her dower that was still owed to her. She said:
"A little provision from a beloved who parts"
When he heard her words, he wept and said: "Had I not heard my grandfather, or my father told me that he heard my grandfather say: 'Any man who divorces his wife three times in an indefinite manner, or three times during her menstrual periods (al-aqra'), she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband, I would have taken her back."

In another narration: the messenger informed him, and he wept and said: "Had I not separated the divorce for her, I would have taken her back. But I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Any man who divorces his wife three times, one divorce at each purity (tuhr), or one divorce at the beginning of each month, or divorces her three times at once, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband.'"

The ninth issue: whoever neglected the mut'ah until years had passed, let him pay it to her, even if she has married, and to her heirs if she has died. This was narrated by Ibn al-Mawwaz from Ibn al-Qasim. Ashhab said: there is nothing upon him if she dies, because it is a consolation to the wife for divorce, and that has now passed. The reasoning of the first view is that it is a right established upon him, and it passes from her to her heirs like other rights. This indicates that it is obligatory in the school.

The tenth issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿upon the wealthy is his measure, and upon the straitened is his measure﴾ is evidence for the obligation of mut'ah. The majority read "al-Musi'i" with a sukun on the waw and a kasra on the sin, meaning the one whose means have widened. It is said: "So-and-so spends according to his measure," meaning according to his capacity. Abu Haywah read it with a fatha on the waw and a shadda and fatha on the sin. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr and 'Asim in the transmission of Abu Bakr read "qadaruhu" with a sukun on the dal in both places. Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and 'Asim in the transmission of Hafs read it with a fatha on the dal in both. Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash and others said: both have the same meaning, two eloquent dialects, and so Abu Zayd related. One says: "take the qadr of such-and-such" and "qadar of such-and-such," with the same meaning. And in the Book of Allah it is read: ﴿so the valleys flowed with their measure﴾ and "qadriha," and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and they did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾. If the dal were vowelled with a kasra, it would also be permissible. "Al-Muqtir" is the one who is poor, the one of little wealth. And "mata'an" is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: provide for them a provision (matta'uhunna mata'an), "according to what is reasonable," that is, according to what is known in the Sharia of moderation.

The eleventh issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿a duty upon the doers of good﴾, meaning that this is due upon them as a duty; one says "haqaqtu 'alayhi al-qada'" and "ahqaqtu," meaning I made it obligatory. In this is evidence for the obligation of mut'ah together with the command to it, so His saying "haqqan" is an emphasis on the obligation. The meaning of "upon the doers of good" and "upon the God-fearing" is upon the believers, since no one may say: "I am neither a doer of good nor God-fearing," and people are commanded to be all doers of good and God-fearing, so they do good by performing Allah's obligations and avoiding His disobediences, so that they do not enter the Fire. Thus it is obligatory upon all creation to be doers of good and God-fearing. And "haqqan" is either an adjective to "mata'an" or is in the accusative as a verbal noun, and that is more emphatic regarding the command. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 237 (part 1 of 2):

There are eight issues concerning this verse.

The First: People have differed concerning this verse. A group, including Malik and others, said: it excludes the divorced woman after the fixing of the dowry from the ruling on providing maintenance (mut'ah), since the Almighty's words ﴿and provide for them﴾ encompass her. Ibn al-Musayyib said: this verse abrogated the verse in Surat al-Ahzab [[verse 49, see vol. 14 p. 202]], because that verse included providing for every woman who had not been consummated with. Qatadah said: this verse abrogated the verse preceding it. I say: the view of Sa'id and Qatadah is open to question, since the conditions of abrogation (naskh) are not present and reconciling the two is possible. Ibn al-Qasim said in al-Mudawwanah: provision was for every divorced woman by the Almighty's words ﴿and for divorced women is provision according to what is reasonable﴾, and for the one not yet consummated with by the verse in Surat al-Ahzab [[verse 49, see vol. 14 p. 202]]. Thus the Almighty singled out, by this verse, the one for whom a dowry had been fixed before consummation, and established for her only half of what was fixed. A group of scholars, among them Abu Thawr, said: the provision (mut'ah) is for every divorced woman in general, and this verse only clarifies that the woman for whom a dowry was fixed takes half of what was fixed for her; the verse did not intend to cancel her provision, rather she has both the provision and half of the fixed dowry.

The Second: The Almighty's words ﴿then half of what you have fixed﴾, meaning: what is obligatory is half of what you have fixed, namely of the dowry; so half is for the husband and half is for the woman, by consensus. Al-nisf (half) is one part of two. It is said: "the water reached half (nasafa) the cup," meaning it reached its half; "the half (nisf) of the waist-wrap is the shin," and whatever reaches half of something else has "nasafa" it. The majority read ﴿fa-nisfu﴾ with a raised (ḍammah) fa'. A group read ﴿fa-nisfa﴾ with the fa' in the accusative, meaning: "then pay half." Ali ibn Abi Talib and Zayd ibn Thabit read ﴿fa-nisfu﴾ with a ḍammah on the nun throughout the Qur'an, and this is a dialect. Al-Asma'i likewise related a reading from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala': it is said nisf, nasf and nasif, three dialectal forms for "half." In a hadith: "If one of you were to spend gold equal to Uhud, it would not reach a mudd of one of them, nor half of it," meaning its half. Al-nasif also means a veil.

The Third: If he gave her a dowry and then divorced her before consummation, and the dowry grew in her hand, Malik said: every item (ʿaraḍ) or slave he gave her, its growth belongs to both of them together, and its loss is between them, and if it is destroyed (tarāhu [[tarāhu: its destruction]]) it falls on both of them together, and the woman bears none of it. If he gave her gold or silver coin and she bought with it a slave or a house, or bought with it perfume, household goods (shiwar [[al-shiwar: household goods]]), or anything else that she is entitled to dispose of for her trousseau and the good of her affairs while she remains with him, all of that is in the position of what he had given her as dowry, and its growth and loss are between them. If he divorces her before consummation, she has only half of it, and she is not obliged to repay him half of what she received from him. If she bought with it, or from it, something for herself exclusively, she must repay him half of the dowry she received from him. Likewise, if she bought from someone else a slave or a house with the thousand he gave her as dowry and then he divorced her before consummation, he has recourse against her for half of the thousand.

The Fourth: There is no disagreement that whoever consummates marriage with his wife and then dies leaving her, and he had named a dowry for her, she is entitled to that named dowry in full and to inheritance, and she observes the waiting period (ʿiddah). They differed concerning a man who was alone with a woman but did not have intercourse with her until he parted from her. The Kufans and Malik said: he owes the full dowry, and she observes the waiting period, on the basis of the report of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The rightly-guided caliphs ruled concerning one who closes a door or lets down a curtain that she is entitled to inheritance and must observe the waiting period." It is also related as a marfu' report, which al-Daraqutni transmitted, and it will come in Surat al-Nisa' [[see vol. 6 p. 102]]. Al-Shafi'i does not oblige a full dowry nor a waiting period when there was no consummation, on the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. Shurayh said: "I have not heard that the Almighty mentioned in His Book a door or a curtain." If he claims that he did not touch her, she has half the dowry, and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas. What our scholars have said on this will come in Surat al-Nisa', God willing, at His words: ﴿and when you have gone in to one another﴾.

The Fifth: His words, exalted is He: ﴿unless they forgo, or he forgoes in whose hand is the marriage tie﴾, to the end of the verse. ﴿Unless they forgo﴾ is an exception of a disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), because their forgoing half is not of the same kind as their receiving it. And ﴿yaʿfuna﴾ means they leave aside and pardon, and its pattern is yafʿalna. The meaning: unless they relinquish the half that became due to them from the husband. The nun was not dropped after "an" (that), because the feminine plural in the imperfect is in one form in the nominative, accusative and jussive; it is a pronoun and not a sign of grammatical case, so it was not dropped, and also because dropping the nun would cause confusion with the masculine. The "forgoing women" in this verse are every woman who controls her own affairs. God the Almighty permitted them to waive it after it became obligatory, since He made it their exclusive right, so they may dispose of it by confirming or waiving as they wish, provided they control their own affairs and are adult, sensible and mature. Ibn 'Abbas, and a group of jurists and of the Successors (tabi'un), said: the forgoing of a virgin who has no guardian is permissible. Sahnun related this in al-Mudawwanah from other than Ibn al-Qasim, after it was mentioned to Ibn al-Qasim that her waiving half the dowry is not permissible. As for one under the guardianship of a father or a guardian (wasi), her waiving half her dowry is not permissible by a single view, and there is no disagreement on this as far as I know.

The Sixth: His words, exalted is He: ﴿or he forgoes in whose hand is the marriage tie﴾ are conjoined with the first and are indeclinable (mabni), while this is declinable (mu'rab). Al-Hasan read "aw yaʿfu" with a sukun on the waw, as if he found the fatha on the waw burdensome. People have differed concerning the intended meaning of His words: "or he forgoes in whose hand is the marriage tie." Al-Daraqutni related from Jubayr ibn Mut'im that he married a woman from Banu Nasr [[so in al-Daraqutni and all manuscripts of the original except h, where it reads Banu Nadir. In al-Taj it is stated that Banu Nasr is a clan of Hawazin.]] and then divorced her before consummation; he sent her the full dowry and said: "I have more right to forgo than she does." He cited the Almighty's words: ﴿unless they forgo, or he forgoes in whose hand is the marriage tie﴾, and said: "and I have more right to forgo than she." He interpreted His words ﴿or he forgoes in whose hand is the marriage tie﴾ as meaning himself, in every case, before and after divorce, that is, the tie of his marriage. When he introduced the lam he omitted the ha', as in His words: ﴿for indeed Paradise is the refuge﴾ [[see vol. 19 p. 205]], meaning its refuge. Al-Nabigha said:

They possess a disposition which God has not given to any other than them,
of generosity and forbearance, not lacking in them.

Namely, their dreams (ahlamuhum). Likewise His saying "the knot of marriage" (ʿuqdat al-nikah) means the knot of his marriage. Al-Daraqutni narrated it as a marfuʿ report (traced directly to the Prophet) from the hadith of Qutaybah ibn Saʿid: Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who holds the knot of marriage is the husband." This has also been attributed to ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Shurayh. He said: Likewise said Nafiʿ ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Tawus, Mujahid, al-Shaʿbi and Saʿid ibn Jubayr; others added Mujahid again and al-Thawri, and Abu Hanifa chose this view, and it is the sound view of al-Shafiʿi. All of them hold that the guardian has no way to any part of her dowry, because of the consensus that if the guardian released the husband from the dowry before divorce, it would not be valid; so likewise after it. And they agreed that the guardian does not have the right to give away any part of her property, and the dowry is her property. And they agreed that among the guardians there are those whose pardon is not valid, namely the paternal cousins and the nephews (sons of brothers); so likewise the father, and Allah knows best. Among them are those who said it is the guardian (al-wali); al-Daraqutni also traced this to Ibn ʿAbbas, and he said: This is the view of Ibrahim, ʿAlqamah and al-Hasan; others added ʿIkrimah, Tawus, ʿAta', Abu al-Zinad, Zayd ibn Aslam, Rabiʿah, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Ibn Shihab, al-Aswad ibn Yazid, al-Shaʿbi, Qatadah, Malik, and al-Shafiʿi in his earlier view. So it is permissible for the father to pardon half the dowry of his virgin daughter when she is divorced, whether or not she has reached menstruation. ʿIsa ibn Dinar said: and he does not return anything of it to her father. The evidence that the intended meaning is the guardian is that Allah, glory be to Him, said at the beginning of the verse: "And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already appointed for them a dowry, then half of what you have appointed" — so He mentioned the husbands and addressed them with this address. Then He said: "unless they pardon" — so He mentioned the women — "or he in whose hand is the knot of marriage pardons," so this is a third party, and it is not referred back to the earlier husband unless there were no other person, and the guardian exists, so he is the intended one. Makki said this meaning, and Ibn al-ʿArabi mentioned it. Also, Allah said: "unless they pardon," and it is known that not every woman can pardon, for a minor girl and a woman under guardianship have no pardon; so Allah clarified the two categories: "unless they pardon," meaning if they are competent for that, "or he in whose hand is the knot of marriage pardons," who is the guardian, because the matter lies with him. Likewise Ibn Wahb, Ashhab, Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam and Ibn al-Qasim narrated from Malik that it is the father regarding his virgin daughter, and the master regarding his slave-woman. The guardian's pardon is valid only if he is of sound judgment, and his pardon is not valid if he is a fool. If it is said: We do not grant that it is the guardian; rather it is the husband, and this title is more appropriate for him, because he has more authority over the contract than the guardian, as previously stated. The answer: We do not grant that the husband has more authority over the contract than the father in his virgin daughter; rather the father alone has it, not the husband, because what is contracted upon is the virgin's womb (buḍʿ), and the husband does not have the right to contract over it; the father has it. Shurayh permitted the pardon of a brother regarding half the dowry, and likewise ʿIkrimah said: the pardon of the one who concluded the knot of marriage between them is permissible, whether he was an uncle, a father or a brother, even if the woman dislikes it. Abu Nuhayk and al-Shaʿbi read "aw yaʿfu" with the waw sukun, by analogy with the alif (al-tashbih), and similar to it is the saying of the poet: "ʿAmir did not make me chief by inheritance; God refused that I should be called by a mother or a father."

The seventh: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that you pardon is nearer to piety﴾. It is a beginning and a predicate; the original is taʿfuwu, the first waw was made sukun because its movement was heavy, then it was deleted because of the meeting of two sukuns. It is addressed to men and women in His saying, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, with the masculine predominating; and the lam means "to" (ila), i.e., nearer to piety. Al-Jumhur read "taʿfū" with the ta' and two dots above. Abu Nuhayk and al-Shaʿbi read "wa-an yaʿfū" with the ya', and that refers back to the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage. I say: He did not read "wa-an taʿfunna" with the ta', which would be for women.

Al-Jumhur read "wa-la tansawu al-fadl" with a damma on the waw, and Yahya ibn Yaʿmur read it with a kasra. ʿAli, Mujahid, Abu Haywa and Ibn Abi ʿAblah read "wa-la tanasaw al-fadl," and this is a reading of firm meaning, because it is a place of mutual forgetting (tanasin), not forgetting, except by analogy. Mujahid said: "the favour" (al-fadl) is the man completing the whole dowry, or the woman leaving the half that is hers.

The eighth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed Allah is seeing of what you do﴾. It is a statement that implicitly contains a promise for the doers of good and deprivation for those who are not doers of good, meaning: your pardon and your complete giving are not hidden from Him.

**Question 1:** In this verse there are eight issues. The first concerns God's words, ﴿Guard (ḥāfiẓū) the prayers﴾. The address is to the whole community, and the verse commands that the prayers be kept up at their appointed times with all their conditions. *Al-muḥāfaẓa* (constancy) means persisting in a thing and being regular in it.

*Al-wusṭā* is the feminine of *al-awsaṭ* (the middlemost). The *wasaṭ* (middle) of a thing is its best and most balanced part. From this comes God's words, ﴿And thus We have made you a middle (wasaṭan) community﴾. This was discussed earlier (see the first question, vol. 2, p. 153). A Bedouin Arab, praising the Prophet ﷺ, said:

*O the most central of people in all their glories,*
*and the most noble of people in mother and father.*

*Waṭṭa* (i.e., *wasṭa* as a verb) is used when someone says, "Such-and-such stood in the midst of the people," meaning he became among them.

God singled out the middle prayer for mention, although it had already been included in the general term "the prayers," in order to honour it. This is like God's words, ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah (see vol. 14, p. 126)﴾, and His words, ﴿In them are fruit, palm trees and pomegranates (see vol. 17, p. 185)﴾.

Abū Ja'far al-Wāsiṭī read *"wal-ṣalāta al-wusṭā"* with the accusative case as an *ighrā'* (an exhortation, meaning "and keep to the middle prayer"). Al-Ḥalwānī also read it this way. Qālūn, from Nāfi', read *"al-wuṣṭā"* with the *ṣād*, because the *ṭā'* is adjacent to it, and the two letters share the same point of articulation. Both forms are dialectal variants, like *al-ṣirāṭ* (for *al-sirāṭ*) and similar words.

**Question 2:** People differed over identifying the middle prayer, and there are ten opinions.

The first opinion is that it is the *Ẓuhr* (noon prayer). This is because it falls in the middle of the day, according to the more accurate of the two views that the day begins at dawn, as explained earlier. We begin with the noon prayer because it was the first prayer performed in Islam. Among those who said it is the middle prayer were Zayd ibn Thābit, Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī, 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Umar and 'Ā'isha, may God be pleased with them all.

One piece of evidence that it is the middle prayer is what 'Ā'isha and Ḥafṣa said when they dictated, *"Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer,"* with a *wāw* (the conjunction "and") between them.

It is also narrated that it was harder on the Muslims than other prayers, because it fell at the hottest time of the day (*al-hājira*), when they had been wearied by their work for their livelihoods. Abū Dāwūd related from Zayd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ used to pray the noon prayer at the hottest time of day, and no prayer was harder on the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ than it. So God revealed: *"Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer."* He said: "Two prayers come before it and two come after it."

Mālik related in his *Muwaṭṭa'*, and Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī in his *Musnad*, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: "The middle prayer is the noon prayer." Al-Ṭayālisī added: "And the Messenger of God ﷺ used to pray it at the hottest time of day (*bil-hajīr*)."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 238 (part 2 of 4):

Second: it is the ʿAṣr (afternoon prayer), because before it are two daytime prayers and after it are two nighttime prayers. Al-Naḥḥas said: "A better argument than this is that it was called the middle (wusṭā) only because it lies between two prayers, one of which was the first to be enjoined and the other the second of those enjoined." Among those who said it is the middle prayer were ʿAlī ibn Abi Ṭalib, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn ʿUmar, Abu Hurayrah and Abu Saʿid al-Khudri. This is the preference of Abu Hanifah and his companions, and it is what al-Shafiʿi and most people of hadith held. ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Habib also adopted it, and Ibn al-ʿArabi preferred it in his al-Qabas, as did Ibn ʿAtiyyah in his tafsir, and he said: "The majority of people hold this view, and I say the same." They cited the hadiths on this subject [[In manuscripts B and H: "hadiths reported."]] which Muslim and others transmitted, the most explicit of which is the hadith of Ibn Masʿud who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the prayer of ʿAṣr." It was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, who said: "A hasan sahih hadith." We have given more on this in al-Qabas, in the commentary on the Muwatta' of Malik ibn Anas.

Third: it is the Maghrib (sunset prayer). This was said by Qabisah ibn Abi Dhuʾayb along with a group. Their argument is that it is intermediate in the number of rakʿahs, being neither the fewest nor the most, and it is not shortened when travelling; and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) neither delayed it beyond its time nor hastened it; and after it come two loud prayers and before it two silent prayers. It is related from the hadith of ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The most excellent of prayers before Allah is the prayer of Maghrib. He does not relieve it from the traveller or the resident. Allah opened the night prayer with it and closed the day prayer with it. Whoever prays Maghrib and then two rakʿahs after it, Allah builds him a palace in Paradise; and whoever prays four rakʿahs after it, Allah forgives him the sins of twenty years, or he said forty years."

Fourth: the ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah (night prayer), because it lies between two prayers that are not shortened, and it occurs at the time of sleep, and it is recommended to delay it, and that is difficult, so emphasis was placed on preserving it.

Fifth: it is the Ṣubḥ (dawn prayer), because before it are two nighttime prayers recited aloud and after it are two daytime prayers recited silently; and because its time begins while people are asleep, and rising for it is hard in the cold of winter and in summer because of the shortness of the night. Among those who said it is the middle prayer were ʿAlī ibn Abi Ṭalib and ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas. Mālik transmitted it in the Muwatta' as a balagh (a report that he had received from them). Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas as taʿlīq (a hadith related without a complete chain). It is also related from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah, and it is the view of Malik and his companions, and al-Shafiʿi's inclination, as al-Qushayri reported from him. The sound report from ʿAlī is that it is the ʿAṣr, and this is related from him through a known and sound channel.

Those who say it is the Ṣubḥ have relied on Allah's words: "And stand before Allah in devotion (qānitīn)," meaning in it, and no obligatory prayer includes qunūt except the Ṣubḥ. Abu Rajaʾ said: "Ibn ʿAbbas led us in the dawn prayer at Basra, and he performed qunūt in it before bowing and raised his hands. When he finished he said: 'This is the middle prayer which Allah commanded us to stand in devotion during.'" Anas said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) performed qunūt in the dawn prayer after bowing." The ruling on qunūt and what the scholars hold concerning it will come in Surat Al ʿImran at His words: "You have no part in the affair at all" [[See vol. 4, p. 199.]].

Sixth: the Friday prayer (Jumuʿah), because it is singled out for congregation, for the khutbah within it, and it is made a festival. This was mentioned by Ibn Habib and Makki. Muslim transmitted from ʿAbdullah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to people who were absent from the Friday prayer: "I have wanted to order a man to lead the people in prayer and then burn the houses of men who stay away from the Friday prayer."

Seventh: it is the Ṣubḥ and the ʿAṣr together. This was said by Shaykh Abu Bakr al-Abhari, who argued with the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Angels take turns among you by night and angels by day," the hadith narrated by Abu Hurayrah. Jarir ibn ʿAbdullah related: "We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'Indeed you will see your Lord just as you see this moon, you will not be wronged [[Al-Nawawi said: "Tuḍāmūn" is read with a doubled mim and with a single mim. Whoever doubles it puts a fatha on the ta', and the meaning of the doubled form is that you do not jostle one another and are gentle in reaching the sight of Him; the meaning of the single form is that no harm (ḍaym), meaning hardship and fatigue, will befall you. In manuscript H: "lā tuḍārūn" (you will not be harmed).]] in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome from a prayer before the rising of the sun and a prayer before its setting'" — meaning the ʿAṣr and the Fajr — "then he recited: 'And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting'" [[See vol. 11, p. 260.]]. ʿAmārah ibn Ruwaybah related: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'None who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will enter the Fire,'" meaning the Fajr and the ʿAṣr. And from him: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays the two cool prayers (al-bardayn) enters Paradise." All of this is established in the Sahih of Muslim and elsewhere. They were called al-bardayn because they are performed at the two cool times.

Eighth: it is the ʿAtamah (late night prayer, i.e. ʿIshāʾ) and the Ṣubḥ. Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, said in the illness of which he died: "Listen and convey to those after you: maintain these two prayers, meaning in congregation, the ʿIshāʾ and the Ṣubḥ. If you knew what is in them you would come to them even crawling on your elbows and knees." This was said by ʿUmar and ʿUthman. The imams related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "If they knew what is in the ʿAtamah and the Ṣubḥ they would come to them, even crawling," and he said: "They are the heaviest of prayers upon the hypocrites." For one who prays the Ṣubḥ in congregation there is the reward of a night's standing (qiyām), and for the ʿAtamah half a night's standing. This was mentioned by Malik as a mawqūf report from ʿUthman, and Muslim transmitted it as marfūʿ. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi transmitted from him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever attends the ʿIshāʾ in congregation has the reward of half a night's standing, and whoever prays the ʿIshāʾ and the Fajr in congregation has the reward of standing the whole night." This contradicts what Malik and Muslim transmitted.

Ninth: it is all five prayers together. Muʿadh ibn Jabal said: because His words "Guard the prayers" (ḥāfiẓū ʿalā al-ṣalawāt) encompass the obligatory and the voluntary, then the obligatory was singled out for mention.

Tenth: it is unspecified. This was said by Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, and said by al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym. Allah concealed it among the prayers as He concealed the Night of Power in Ramadan, and as He concealed the hour on Friday and the hours of the night in which supplication is answered, so that people would stand in the night in the darkness to commune with the Knower of the unseen. Among what shows that it is indeterminate and unspecified is what Muslim transmitted in his Sahih at the end of the chapter from al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib, who said: "This verse was revealed: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the ʿAṣr,' and we recited it as long as Allah willed. Then Allah abrogated it, and it was revealed: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer.'" A man said: "So it is the ʿAṣr?" Al-Baraʾ said: "I have told you how it was revealed and how Allah abrogated it, and Allah knows best." It follows from this that after it had been specified, its specification was abrogated and it was made indeterminate, so the specification was lifted, and Allah knows best. This is the choice of Muslim, since he placed it at the end of the chapter, and more than one of the later scholars held it, and it is the sound view, Allah willing, because the evidences conflict and there is no preponderance, so nothing remains but to preserve all of them and perform each at its time, and Allah knows best.

Third issue: this difference concerning the middle prayer shows the invalidity of whoever affirmed the words "and the prayer of ʿAṣr" mentioned in the hadith of Abu Yunus, mawla of ʿAʾishah, when she ordered him to write for her a copy of the Qur'an. Our scholars said: that was only like an explanation from the Prophet (ﷺ). This is shown by the hadith of ʿAmr ibn Rafiʿ who said: Ḥafṣah ordered me to write for her a copy, the hadith... and in it: she dictated to me "Guard the prayers and the middle prayer — which is the ʿAṣr — and stand before Allah in devotion," and she said: "This is how I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it." Her words "which is the ʿAṣr" are evidence that the Prophet (ﷺ) explained the middle prayer within the words of Allah by saying "which is the ʿAṣr." Nafiʿ related from Ḥafṣah "and the prayer of ʿAṣr," as was related from ʿAʾishah, and from Ḥafṣah also "the prayer of ʿAṣr" without the waw. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: this disagreement over this added wording shows its invalidity and the soundness of what is in the Imam, the codex of the Muslim community. There is another argument against it: whoever says "and the middle prayer and the prayer of ʿAṣr" makes the middle prayer other than ʿAṣr, and this contradicts the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) which ʿAbdullah related: "The polytheists kept the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) busy on the day of the Confederates from the prayer of ʿAṣr until the sun turned yellow, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'They kept us busy from the middle prayer; may Allah fill their bellies and their graves with fire.'" [[In manuscripts B and Z: "What is wrong with them, may Allah fill..." In Ibn ʿAtiyyah and al-Bahr: "They kept us busy from the middle prayer, the prayer of ʿAṣr." In Ibn ʿAtiyyah: "may Allah fill their graves and houses..." In al-Bahr: "may Allah fill their bellies..."]] The hadith.

Fourth issue: the words of Allah (and the middle prayer) show that the witr is not obligatory, because the Muslims agreed that the number of obligatory prayers is not less than five and not more than... and there is no odd number between three and seven except five, and even numbers have no middle; so it is established that they are five. In the hadith of the Night Journey: "They are five and they are fifty; the word is not changed before Me."

Fifth issue: His words "and stand before Allah in devotion" (qānitīn) mean in your prayer. People differed about the meaning of "qānitīn." Al-Shaʿbi said: obedient. Jabir ibn Zayd, ʿAṭāʾ and Saʿid ibn Jubayr [said similarly]. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: every qunūt in the Qur'an means obedience, and Abu Saʿid said it from the Prophet (ﷺ). The people of every religion now stand disobedient, so it was said to this community: stand before Allah obedient. Mujahid said: the meaning of qānitīn is humble (khāshiʿīn). Qunūt is the lengthening of bowing, humility, lowering the gaze and lowering the wing. Al-Rabiʿ said: qunūt is the lengthening of standing, and Ibn ʿUmar said it, and he recited: "Is one who is devoutly (qānit) worshipping in the hours of the night, prostrating and standing" [[See vol. 15, p. 238.]]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best prayer is the lengthy qunūt," related by Muslim and others. And the poet said:

Devout before Allah, calling on his Lord,
And apart from people in solitude.

وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ [راجع المسألة الخامسة ج ٢ ص ٨٦.]. وَرُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّ "قانِتِينَ" بمعنى دَاعِينَ. وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: قَنَتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ شَهْرًا يَدْعُو عَلَى رِعْلٍ وَذَكْوَانَ [رعل وذكوان: قبيلتان من سليم، وإنما دعا عليهم لقتلهم القراء.]. قَالَ قَوْمٌ: مَعْنَاهُ دَعَا، وَقَالَ قَوْمٌ: مَعْنَاهُ طَوَّلَ قِيَامَهُ. وَقَالَ السُّدِّيُّ: "قانِتِينَ" سَاكِتِينَ، دَلِيلُهُ أَنَّ الْآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ فِي الْمَنْعِ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ، وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ مُبَاحًا فِي صَدْرِ الْإِسْلَامِ، وَهَذَا هُوَ الصَّحِيحُ لِمَا رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ وَغَيْرُهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ: كُنَّا نُسَلِّمُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَهُوَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فَيَرُدُّ عَلَيْنَا، فَلَمَّا رَجَعْنَا مِنْ عِنْدِ النَّجَاشِيِّ سَلَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ فَلَمْ يَرُدَّ عَلَيْنَا، فَقُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، كُنَّا نُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْكَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فَتَرُدُّ عَلَيْنَا؟ فَقَالَ: "إِنَّ فِي الصَّلَاةِ شُغْلًا". وَرَوَى زَيْدُ بْنُ أَرْقَمَ قَالَ: كُنَّا نَتَكَلَّمُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ، يُكَلِّمُ الرَّجُلُ صَاحِبَهُ وَهُوَ إِلَى جَنْبِهِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ، حَتَّى نَزَلَتْ: ﴿وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ﴾ فَأُمِرْنَا بِالسُّكُوتِ وَنُهِينَا عَنِ الْكَلَامِ. وَقِيلَ: إِنَّ أَصْلَ الْقُنُوتِ فِي اللُّغَةِ الدَّوَامُ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ. وَمِنْ حَيْثُ كَانَ أَصْلُ الْقُنُوتِ فِي اللُّغَةِ الدَّوَامَ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ جَازَ أَنْ يُسَمَّى مُدِيمُ الطَّاعَةِ قَانِتًا، وَكَذَلِكَ مَنْ أَطَالَ الْقِيَامَ وَالْقِرَاءَةَ وَالدُّعَاءَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ، أَوْ أَطَالَ الْخُشُوعَ وَالسُّكُوتَ، فَكُلُّ هَؤُلَاءِ فَاعِلُونَ لِلْقُنُوتِ.

السَّادِسَةُ- قَالَ أَبُو عُمَرَ: أَجْمَعَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ طُرًّا (جميعًا) أَنَّ الْكَلَامَ عَامِدًا فِي الصَّلَاةِ، إِذَا كَانَ الْمُصَلِّي يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ فِي صَلَاةٍ، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ فِي إِصْلَاحِ صَلَاتِهِ، أَنَّهُ يُفْسِدُ الصَّلَاةَ، إِلَّا مَا رُوِيَ عَنِ الْأَوْزَاعِيِّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: مَنْ تَكَلَّمَ لِإِحْيَاءِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ مِثْلِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْأُمُورِ الْجِسَامِ لَمْ تَفْسُدْ صَلَاتُهُ بِذَلِكَ. وَهُوَ قَوْلٌ ضَعِيفٌ فِي النَّظَرِ، لِقَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ﴿وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ﴾ وَقَالَ زَيْدُ بْنُ أَرْقَمَ: كُنَّا نَتَكَلَّمُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ حَتَّى نَزَلَتْ: ﴿وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ﴾ الْحَدِيثَ. وَقَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ: "إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْدَثَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ أَلَّا تَتَكَلَّمُوا فِي الصَّلَاةِ". وَلَيْسَ الْحَادِثُ الْجَسِيمُ الَّذِي يَجِبُ لَهُ قَطْعُ الصَّلَاةِ، وَمِنْ أَجْلِهِ يُمْنَعُ مِنَ الِاسْتِئْنَافِ، فَمَنْ قَطَعَ صَلَاتَهُ لِمَا يَرَاهُ مِنَ الْفَضْلِ فِي إِحْيَاءِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ مَالٍ أَوْ مَا كَانَ بِسَبِيلِ ذَلِكَ اسْتَأْنَفَ صَلَاتَهُ وَلَمْ يَبْنِ. هَذَا هُوَ الصَّحِيحُ فِي الْمَسْأَلَةِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.

السَّابِعَةُ- وَاخْتَلَفُوا فِي الْكَلَامِ سَاهِيًا فِيهَا، فَذَهَبَ مَالِكٌ وَالشَّافِعِيُّ وَأَصْحَابُهُمَا إِلَى أَنَّ الْكَلَامَ فِيهَا سَاهِيًا لَا يُفْسِدُهَا، غَيْرَ أَنَّ مَالِكًا قَالَ: لَا يُفْسِدُ الصَّلَاةَ تَعَمُّدُ الْكَلَامِ فِيهَا إذا كان في شأنها وإصلاحها، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ رَبِيعَةَ وَابْنِ الْقَاسِمِ. وَرَوَى سَحْنُونُ عَنِ ابْنِ الْقَاسِمِ عَنْ مَالِكٍ قَالَ: لَوْ أَنَّ قَوْمًا صَلَّى بِهِمُ الْإِمَامُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَسَلَّمَ سَاهِيًا، فَسَبَّحُوا بِهِ فَلَمْ يَفْقَهْ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ مِمَّنْ هُوَ مَعَهُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ: إِنَّكَ لَمْ تُتِمَّ فَأَتِمَّ صَلَاتَكَ، فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَى الْقَوْمِ فَقَالَ: أَحَقٌّ مَا يَقُولُ هَذَا؟ فَقَالُوا: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: يُصَلِّي بِهِمُ الْإِمَامُ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ، وَيُصَلُّونَ مَعَهُ بَقِيَّةَ صَلَاتِهِمْ، مَنْ تَكَلَّمَ مِنْهُمْ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ، وَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَيَفْعَلُونَ فِي ذَلِكَ مَا فَعَلَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يَوْمَ ذِي الْيَدَيْنِ [ذو اليدين اسمه الخرباق، وقد كان يصلي خلف النبي ﷺ فَانْصَرَفَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ مِنِ اثْنَتَيْنِ - وكانت رباعية - فقال له ذو اليدين: أقصرت الصلاة أم نسيت يا رسول الله؟ ... إلخ.]. هَذَا قَوْلُ ابْنِ الْقَاسِمِ فِي [كِتَابِهِ [من ب وهـ.]] الْمُدَوَّنَةِ وَرِوَايَتِهِ عَنْ مَالِكٍ، وَهُوَ الْمَشْهُورُ مِنْ مَذْهَبِ مَالِكٍ، وَإِيَّاهُ تَقَلَّدَ إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، وَاحْتَجَّ لَهُ فِي كِتَابِ رَدِّهِ عَلَى مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ. وَذَكَرَ الْحَارِثُ بْنُ مِسْكِينَ قَالَ: أَصْحَابُ مَالِكٍ كُلُّهُمْ عَلَى خِلَافِ قَوْلِ مَالِكٍ فِي مَسْأَلَةِ ذِي الْيَدَيْنِ إِلَّا ابْنَ الْقَاسِمِ وَحْدَهُ، فَإِنَّهُ يَقُولُ فِيهَا بِقَوْلِ مَالِكٍ، وَغَيْرُهُمْ يَأْبَوْنَهُ وَيَقُولُونَ: إِنَّمَا كَانَ هَذَا فِي صَدْرِ الْإِسْلَامِ، فَأَمَّا الْآنَ فَقَدْ عَرَفَ النَّاسُ صَلَاتَهُمْ، فَمَنْ تَكَلَّمَ فِيهَا أَعَادَهَا. وَهَذَا هُوَ قَوْلُ الْعِرَاقِيِّينَ: أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ وَالثَّوْرِيِّ، فَإِنَّهُمْ ذَهَبُوا إِلَى أَنَّ الْكَلَامَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ يُفْسِدُهَا عَلَى أَيِّ حَالٍ كَانَ، سَهْوًا أَوْ عَمْدًا، لِصَلَاحِ صَلَاةٍ كَانَ أَوْ لِغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ النَّخَعِيِّ وَعَطَاءٍ وَالْحَسَنِ وَحَمَّادِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلَيْمَانَ وَقَتَادَةَ.
وَزَعَمَ أَصْحَابُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ أَنَّ حَدِيثَ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ هَذَا فِي قِصَّةِ ذِي الْيَدَيْنِ مَنْسُوخٌ بِحَدِيثِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَزَيْدِ بْنِ أَرْقَمَ، قَالُوا: وَإِنْ كَانَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ مُتَأَخِّرَ الْإِسْلَامِ فَإِنَّهُ أَرْسَلَ حَدِيثَ ذِي الْيَدَيْنِ كَمَا أَرْسَلَ حَدِيثَ "مَنْ أَدْرَكَهُ الْفَجْرُ جُنُبًا فَلَا صَوْمَ لَهُ". قَالُوا: وَكَانَ كَثِيرَ الْإِرْسَالِ.
وَذَكَرَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ زِيَادٍ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو قُرَّةَ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ مَالِكًا يَقُولُ: يُسْتَحَبُّ إِذَا تَكَلَّمَ الرَّجُلُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ أَنْ يَعُودَ لَهَا وَلَا يَبْنِيَ. قَالَ: وَقَالَ لَنَا مَالِكٌ: إِنَّمَا تَكَلَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَتَكَلَّمَ أَصْحَابُهُ مَعَهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ، لِأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّوا أَنَّ الصَّلَاةَ قَصُرَتْ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ لِأَحَدٍ الْيَوْمَ.
وَقَدْ رَوَى سَحْنُونُ عَنِ ابْنِ الْقَاسِمِ فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ فَفَرَغَ عِنْدَ نَفْسِهِ مِنَ الْأَرْبَعِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ إِلَى جَنْبِهِ: إِنَّكَ لَمْ تُصَلِّ إِلَّا ثَلَاثًا، فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَى آخَرَ فَقَالَ: أَحَقٌّ مَا يقوله هَذَا؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: تَفْسُدُ صَلَاتُهُ، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ وَلَا أَنْ يَلْتَفِتَ إِلَيْهِ.
قَالَ أَبُو عُمَرَ: فَكَانُوا يُفَرِّقُونَ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ بَيْنَ الْإِمَامِ مَعَ الْجَمَاعَةِ وَالْمُنْفَرِدِ، فَيُجِيزُونَ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ فِي شَأْنِ الصَّلَاةِ لِلْإِمَامِ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ مَا لَا يُجِيزُونَهُ لِلْمُنْفَرِدِ، وَكَانَ غَيْرُ هَؤُلَاءِ يَحْمِلُونَ جَوَابَ ابْنِ الْقَاسِمِ فِي الْمُنْفَرِدِ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ، وَفِي الْإِمَامِ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ، عَلَى اخْتِلَافٍ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ فِي اسْتِعْمَالِ حَدِيثِ ذِي الْيَدَيْنِ، كَمَا اخْتَلَفَ قَوْلُ مَالِكٍ فِي ذَلِكَ.
وَقَالَ الشَّافِعِيُّ وَأَصْحَابُهُ: مَنْ تَعَمَّدَ الْكَلَامَ وَهُوَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُتِمَّ الصَّلَاةَ، وَأَنَّهُ فِيهَا، أَفْسَدَ صَلَاتَهُ، فَإِنْ تَكَلَّمَ سَاهِيًا، أَوْ تَكَلَّمَ وَهُوَ يَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ لِأَنَّهُ قَدْ أَكْمَلَهَا عِنْدَ نَفْسِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ يَبْنِي.
وَاخْتَلَفَ قَوْلُ أَحْمَدَ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ، فَذَكَرَ الْأَثْرَمُ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: مَا تَكَلَّمَ بِهِ الْإِنْسَانُ فِي صَلَاتِهِ لِإِصْلَاحِهَا لَمْ تَفْسُدْ عَلَيْهِ صَلَاتُهُ، فَإِنْ تَكَلَّمَ لِغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَسَدَتْ، وَهَذَا هُوَ قَوْلُ مَالِكٍ الْمَشْهُورُ.
وَذَكَرَ الْخِرَقِيُّ [الخرقي (بكسر الخاء المعجمة وفتح الراء): أبو القاسم عمر بن الحسين شيخ الحنابلة.] عَنْهُ أَنَّ مَذْهَبَهُ فِيمَنْ تَكَلَّمَ عَامِدًا أَوْ سَاهِيًا بَطَلَتْ صَلَاتُهُ، إِلَّا الْإِمَامَ خَاصَّةً، فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا تَكَلَّمَ لِمَصْلَحَةِ صَلَاتِهِ لَمْ تَبْطُلْ صَلَاتُهُ.
وَاسْتَثْنَى سَحْنُونُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ مَالِكٍ أَنَّ مَنْ سَلَّمَ مِنَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فِي الرُّبَاعِيَّةِ فَوَقَعَ الْكَلَامُ هُنَاكَ لَمْ تَبْطُلِ الصَّلَاةُ، وَإِنْ وَقَعَ فِي غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ بَطَلَتِ الصَّلَاةُ.
وَالصَّحِيحُ مَا ذَهَبَ إِلَيْهِ مَالِكٌ فِي الْمَشْهُورِ، تَمَسُّكًا بِالْحَدِيثِ، وَحَمْلًا لَهُ عَلَى الْأَصْلِ الْكُلِّيِّ مِنْ تَعَدِّي الْأَحْكَامِ وَعُمُومِ الشَّرِيعَةِ، وَدَفْعًا لِمَا يُتَوَهَّمُ مِنَ الْخُصُوصِيَّةِ، إِذْ لَا دَلِيلَ عَلَيْهَا.
فَإِنْ قَالَ قَائِلٌ: فَقَدْ جَرَى الْكَلَامُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَالسَّهْوُ أَيْضًا، وَقَدْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ لَهُمْ: "التَّسْبِيحُ لِلرِّجَالِ وَالتَّصْفِيقُ لِلنِّسَاءِ" فَلِمَ لَمْ يُسَبِّحُوا؟
فَقَالَ: لَعَلَّ فِي ذَلِكَ الوقت لم يكن أمرهم بذلك، وَلَئِنْ كَانَ كَمَا ذَكَرْتَ فَلَمْ يُسَبِّحُوا، لِأَنَّهُمْ تَوَهَّمُوا أَنَّ الصَّلَاةَ قَصُرَتْ، وَقَدْ جَاءَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ قَالَ: وَخَرَجَ سَرَعَانُ [السرعان (بفتح السين والراء ويجوز تسكين الراء): أوائل الناس الذين يتسابقون إلى الشيء ويقبلون عليه بسرعة.] النَّاسِ فَقَالُوا: أَقَصُرَتِ الصَّلَاةُ؟ فَلَمْ يَكُنْ بُدٌّ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ لِأَجْلِ ذَلِكَ. وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَقَدْ قَالَ بَعْضُ الْمُخَالِفِينَ: قَوْلُ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ "صَلَّى بِنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ" يَحْتَمِلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُرَادُهُ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى بِالْمُسْلِمِينَ وَهُوَ لَيْسَ مِنْهُمْ، كَمَا رُوِيَ عَنِ النَّزَّالِ [في ب وهـ: البراء بن عازب وليس بشيء. والصواب ما أثبتنا عن الجصاص ج ١ ص ٤٤٦ وفي كل الأصول: حديث البراء. وهو خطأ.] بْنِ سَبْرَةَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: قَالَ لَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: "أَنَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ كُنَّا نُدْعَى بَنِي عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ، وَأَنْتُمُ الْيَوْمَ بَنُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، وَنَحْنُ بَنُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ" وَإِنَّمَا عَنَى بِهِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ، وَهَذَا بَعِيدٌ، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَقُولَ "صَلَّى بِنَا" وَهُوَ إِذْ ذَاكَ كَافِرٌ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الصَّلَاةِ، وَيَكُونُ ذَلِكَ كَذِبًا، وَحَدِيثُ النَّزَّالِ [في ب وهـ: البراء بن عازب وليس بشيء. والصواب ما أثبتنا عن الجصاص ج ١ ص ٤٤٦ وفي كل الأصول: حديث البراء. وهو خطأ.] هُوَ كَانَ مِنْ جُمْلَةِ الْقَوْمِ وَسَمِعَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ مَا سَمِعَ.
وَأَمَّا مَا ادَّعَتْهُ الْحَنَفِيَّةُ مِنَ النَّسْخِ وَالْإِرْسَالِ، فَقَدْ أَجَابَ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ عُلَمَاؤُنَا وَغَيْرُهُمْ وَأَبْطَلُوهُ، وَخَاصَّةً الْحَافِظُ أَبُو عُمَرَ ابْنُ عَبْدِ الْبَرِّ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْمُسَمَّى بِ "التَّمْهِيدِ"، وَذَكَرَ أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ أَسْلَمَ عَامَ خَيْبَرَ، وَقَدِمَ الْمَدِينَةَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْعَامِ، وَصَحِبَ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ أَرْبَعَةَ أَعْوَامٍ، وَشَهِدَ قِصَّةَ ذِي الْيَدَيْنِ وَحَضَرَهَا، وَأَنَّهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ قَبْلَ بَدْرٍ كَمَا زَعَمُوا، وَأَنَّ ذَا الْيَدَيْنِ قُتِلَ فِي بَدْرٍ.
قَالَ: وَحُضُورُ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ يَوْمَ ذِي الْيَدَيْنِ مَحْفُوظٌ مِنْ رِوَايَةِ الْحُفَّاظِ الثِّقَاتِ، وَلَيْسَ تَقْصِيرُ مَنْ قَصَّرَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ بِحُجَّةٍ عَلَى مَنْ عَلِمَ ذَلِكَ وَحَفِظَهُ وَذَكَرَهُ.

الثَّامِنَةُ- الْقُنُوتُ: الْقِيَامُ، وَهُوَ أَحَدُ أَقْسَامِهِ فِيمَا ذَكَرَ أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ الْأَنْبَارِيِّ. وَأَجْمَعَتِ الْأُمَّةُ عَلَى أَنَّ الْقِيَامَ فِي صَلَاةِ الْفَرْضِ وَاجِبٌ عَلَى كُلِّ صَحِيحٍ قَادِرٍ عَلَيْهِ، مُنْفَرِدًا كَانَ أَوْ إِمَامًا.
وَقَالَ ﷺ: "إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ الْإِمَامُ لِيُؤْتَمَّ بِهِ، فَإِذَا صَلَّى قَائِمًا فَصَلُّوا قِيَامًا" الْحَدِيثَ، أَخْرَجَهُ الْأَئِمَّةُ، وَهُوَ بَيَانٌ لِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ﴾.
وَاخْتَلَفُوا فِي الْمَأْمُومِ الصَّحِيحِ يُصَلِّي قَاعِدًا خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ مَرِيضٍ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ الْقِيَامَ، فَأَجَازَتْ ذَلِكَ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ، بَلْ جُمْهُورُهُمْ، لِقَوْلِهِ ﷺ فِي الْإِمَامِ: "وَإِذَا صَلَّى جَالِسًا فَصَلُّوا جُلُوسًا أَجْمَعُونَ"، وَهَذَا هُوَ الصَّحِيحُ فِي الْمَسْأَلَةِ عَلَى مَا نُبَيِّنُهُ آنِفًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.
وَقَدْ أَجَازَ طَائِفَةٌ مِنَ الْعُلَمَاءِ صَلَاةَ الْقَائِمِ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ الْمَرِيضِ، لِأَنَّ كُلًّا يُؤَدِّي فَرْضَهُ عَلَى قَدْرِ طَاقَتِهِ، تَأَسِّيًا بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذْ صَلَّى فِي مَرَضِهِ الَّذِي تُوُفِّيَ فِيهِ قَاعِدًا وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ إِلَى جَنْبِهِ قَائِمًا يُصَلِّي بِصَلَاتِهِ، وَالنَّاسُ قِيَامٌ خَلْفَهُ، وَلَمْ يُشِرْ إِلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَلَا إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْجُلُوسِ، وَأَكْمَلَ صَلَاتَهُ بِهِمْ جَالِسًا وَهُمْ قِيَامٌ، وَمَعْلُومٌ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ كَانَ مِنْهُ بَعْدَ سُقُوطِهِ عَنْ فَرَسِهِ، فَعُلِمَ أَنَّ الْآخِرَ مِنْ فِعْلِهِ نَاسِخٌ لِلْأَوَّلِ.
قَالَ أَبُو عُمَرَ: وَمِمَّنْ ذَهَبَ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَذْهَبِ وَاحْتَجَّ بِهَذِهِ الْحُجَّةِ الشَّافِعِيُّ وَدَاوُدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، وَهِيَ رِوَايَةُ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مَالِكٍ قَالَ: وَأَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ أَنْ يَقُومَ [في ح: "أن يقوم بجنبه".] إِلَى جَنْبِهِ مِمَّنْ يُعْلِمُ النَّاسَ بِصَلَاتِهِ، وَهَذِهِ الرِّوَايَةُ غَرِيبَةٌ عَنْ مَالِكٍ.
وَقَالَ بِهَذَا جَمَاعَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ، وَهُوَ الصَّحِيحُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى، لِأَنَّهَا آخِرُ صَلَاةٍ صَلَّاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ.
وَالْمَشْهُورُ عَنْ مَالِكٍ أَنَّهُ لَا يَؤُمُّ الْقُيَّامَ أَحَدٌ جَالِسًا، فَإِنْ أَمَّهُمْ قَاعِدًا بَطَلَتْ صَلَاتُهُ وَصَلَاتُهُمْ، لِأَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: "لَا يَؤُمَّنَّ أَحَدٌ بَعْدِي قَاعِدًا".
قَالَ:

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 2, verse 238 (part 4 of 4):

If the imam is ill, the imam's prayer is valid, but the prayer of those behind him is invalid.

He said:

"And whoever prays seated without an excuse must repeat the prayer." This is the narration of Abu Mus'ab in his Mukhtasar from Malik. According to it, whoever prays seated must repeat the prayer both within the time and after it.

It has also been narrated from Malik on this matter that they repeat only within the time (al-waqt, the prescribed time), and the position of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan on this is like the well-known position of Malik.

He argued for his position and school with the hadith mentioned by Abu Mus'ab, which al-Daraqutni transmitted from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"No one shall lead the prayer after me while seated."

Al-Daraqutni said: No one narrated it except Jabir al-Ju'fi from al-Sha'bi, and he is abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith), and it is mursal (a hadith whose chain omits the Companion), and no proof is established by it.

Abu 'Umar said: Jabir al-Ju'fi is not to be relied upon for anything he narrates with a complete chain, so how about what he narrates as mursal?

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: If the sick imam prays seated with healthy people and sick people sitting, then his prayer and the prayer of those behind him who are unable to stand is sound and valid, and the prayer of those behind him whose ruling is standing is void.

Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf said: His prayer and their prayer is valid.

They also said: If he prays by gesture (yumi'u) with people who bow and prostrate, it does not suffice them according to all of them, but the imam's prayer is valid.

Zufar used to say: Their prayer suffices them, because they prayed according to their obligation and their imam prayed according to his obligation, as al-Shafi'i said.

I say: As for what Abu 'Umar and others before and after him mentioned, that this was the last prayer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed, I have seen, among others, someone who gathered the chains of the hadiths on this subject, discussed them, and mentioned the disagreement of the jurists on it. We will mention what he mentioned in summary so that the correct view becomes clear to you, God willing, Exalted is He.

The soundness of the view of those who say that the prayer of a healthy follower seated behind a sick imam is valid: Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hibban al-Busti mentioned in his Musnad al-Sahih, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among a group of his Companions and said:

"Do you not know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you?"

They said: "Yes, we bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah!"

He said: "Do you not know that whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and that obedience to Allah is obedience to me?"

They said: "Yes, we bear witness that whoever obeys you has obeyed Allah, and that obedience to Allah is your obedience."

He said: "Indeed, among the obedience to Allah is that you obey me, and among my obedience is that you obey your leaders. If they pray seated, then pray seated."

In its chain is 'Uqba ibn Abi al-Sahba', and he is trustworthy (thiqah), said Yahya ibn Ma'in.

Abu Hatim said: In this report there is clear explanation that the prayer of the followers seated when their imam prays seated is part of the obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which Allah commanded His servants, and in my view it is a kind of consensus (ijma') which they agreed to permit, because among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were four who issued fatwas according to it:

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, Abu Hurayrah, Usayd ibn Hudayr, and Qays ibn Qahd [[Qahd with a qaf, and at its end a dal.]]. No report has been transmitted from any of the Companions who witnessed the descent of revelation and the sending down, and who were protected from distortion and alteration, opposing these four, neither with a connected chain nor a disconnected one. So it is as if the Companions agreed that when the imam prays seated, the followers must pray seated.

Jabir ibn Zayd, al-Awza'i, Malik ibn Anas, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Abu Ayyub Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi, Abu Khaythamah, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Isma'il, and those who followed them from the people of hadith, such as Muhammad ibn Nasr and Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah, also said this.

This sunnah was narrated from the Chosen One (ﷺ) by Anas ibn Malik, 'A'ishah, Abu Hurayrah, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Abu Umamah al-Bahili.

The first in this community to invalidate the prayer of a follower seated when his imam prays seated was al-Mughirah ibn Miqsam, companion of al-Nakha'i. Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman took from him, then Abu Hanifa took from Hammad, and those after him among his companions followed him in it.

The strongest thing they relied upon in this is what Jabir al-Ju'fi narrated from al-Sha'bi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one shall lead the prayer after me while seated." Even if its chain were sound, it would be mursal, and the mursal report and the unnarrated one are equal in ruling according to us. Furthermore, Abu Hanifa says: "I have not seen among those I met anyone better than 'Ata', nor among those I met anyone more of a liar than Jabir al-Ju'fi. Whenever I brought him any opinion (ra'y), he would bring me a hadith about it, and he claimed that he had so-and-so thousand hadiths from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he never uttered." So here Abu Hanifa criticizes Jabir al-Ju'fi and calls him a liar, contrary to the view of those among his companions who ascribed to his school.

Abu Hatim said: As for the prayer of the Prophet (ﷺ) during his illness, the reports about it came in general and brief form, and some of them are detailed and explained. In some of them:

"The Prophet (ﷺ) came [and sat [[In B.]]] beside Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr was following the Prophet (ﷺ), and the people were following Abu Bakr."

In some of them: "He sat to the left of Abu Bakr," and this is explicit.

And in it: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was leading the people seated, while Abu Bakr stood."

Abu Hatim said: As for the summary of this report, 'A'ishah related this prayer up to this point, and the end of the story is in the narration of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah: that the Prophet (ﷺ) also commanded them to sit in this prayer, just as he had commanded them when he fell from his horse. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Qutaybah informed us, saying: Yazid ibn Mawhab informed us, saying: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to me from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said:

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill, and we prayed behind him while he was seated, and Abu Bakr was making the takbir audible to the people." He said: "He turned to us, saw us standing, and gestured to us, so we sat, and we prayed with his prayer seated. When he finished the prayer he said: 'You almost did what the Persians and Romans do, standing before their kings while they sit. So do not do that. Follow your imams: if he prays standing, then pray standing, and if he prays seated, then pray seated.'"

Abu Hatim said: In this explained report there is clear explanation that when the Prophet (ﷺ) sat to the left of Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr moved to be a follower, following his prayer and saying the takbir audibly so the people could follow his prayer, the Prophet (ﷺ) then commanded them to sit when he saw them standing, and when he finished his prayer he also commanded them to sit when their imam prays seated.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah had witnessed the prayer of the Prophet (ﷺ) when he fell from his horse and his right side was scraped (jahash, meaning the skin was torn). His fall (ﷺ) was in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah at the end of the fifth year after the Hijrah. He witnessed this prayer during his illness (ﷺ) at a different time, and so he transmitted each report in its own wording. Do you not see that he mentions in this prayer: "Abu Bakr raised his voice with the takbir so that the people would follow him." And that prayer which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed in his house at the time of his fall from his horse did not require him to raise his voice with the takbir so that the people could hear his takbir, given the smallness of 'A'ishah's room. Rather, his raising his voice with the takbir was in the great mosque, where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed during his illness. When what we have described is established, it is not permissible to make some of these reports abrogate others. This prayer, its going out to it (ﷺ) was between two men, and he led them in it seated and commanded them to sit.

As for the prayer he prayed at the end of his life, his going out to it was between Barirah and Thawbah [[So it is in most of the manuscripts, and in some of them: Thuwaybah, with the triangular letter. The correct form is what is in Ibn Hajar's commentary on al-Bukhari: Barirah and Nawbah, with a damma on the nun, sukun on the waw, then a single ba; Ibn Makula recorded it... see there vol. 8 p. 108, Bulaq edition, where the disagreement and reconciliation are found. As for Thuwaybah, his wet-nurse, peace be upon him, no one has claimed that she was a companion or that she embraced Islam according to the well-known view.]], and in it he was a follower, and he prayed seated behind Abu Bakr, wrapped in a single garment.

Anas ibn Malik narrated: "The last prayer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with the people was in a single garment, wrapped in it, seated behind Abu Bakr." So he (peace be upon him) prayed two prayers in the mosque in congregation, not one prayer.

And in the report of 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah from 'A'ishah: the Prophet (ﷺ) went out between two men, meaning one of them al-'Abbas and the other 'Ali.

And in the report of Masruq from 'A'ishah: "Then the Prophet (ﷺ) felt some lightness, so he went out between Barirah and Thawbah. I was looking at his sandals dragging in the pebbles and looking at the soles of his feet..." the hadith.

This shows you that they were two prayers, not one prayer.

Abu Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'A'ishah: that Abu Bakr led the people in prayer while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the row behind him.

Abu Hatim said: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj differed from Za'idah ibn Qudamah in the text of this report from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah. Shu'bah made the Prophet (ﷺ) a follower when he prayed seated while the people were standing, and Za'idah made the Prophet (ﷺ) an imam when he prayed seated while the people were standing. Both are precise and reliable memorizers.

How is it permissible to make one of the two reports, which appear to contradict each other regarding a single act, an abrogation of a previous general command?

Whoever makes one of the two reports abrogate what preceded from the command of the Prophet (ﷺ) and leaves the other without any evidence established for its soundness, has permitted his opponent to take what he left of the two reports and leave what he took from them.

A parallel to this type of sunnah is the report of Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) married Maymunah while he was in ihram, and the report of Abu Rafi' that the Prophet (ﷺ) married her while they were both free of ihram. The two reports appear to contradict each other regarding a single act, though according to us there is no contradiction between them. A group of the people of hadith made the two reports about the marriage of Maymunah contradictory, and they went to the report of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man in ihram neither marries nor is married," and they took it, since it agrees with one of the two reports narrated about the marriage of Maymunah, and they left the report of Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) married her while he was in ihram. Whoever does this must say: the two reports contradict each other regarding the Prophet's prayer during his illness, according to what we mentioned before. Therefore he must turn to the report containing the command for followers to pray seated when their imam prays seated, and take it, since it agrees with one of the two reports narrated about the Prophet's prayer during his illness, and leave the report that stands alone apart from them, as he did in the marriage of Maymunah.

Abu Hatim said: Some Iraqis who adhered to the school of the Kufans claimed that his saying: "If he prays seated, then pray seated," meant: "If he sits for the tashahhud, then say the tashahhud seated, all of you." Thus he distorted the report from the generality in which it came, without any established evidence for that interpretation.

**Issue 1:** In it are nine issues.

**The first issue:** God's words, ﴿If you fear﴾, from *al-khawf* (fear), which is alarm.

**(*fa-rijalan*)**, meaning: pray on foot.

**(*aw rukbanan*)** is coordinated with it. *Rijal* is the plural of *rajil* or *rajul*, from the saying "*rajila al-insan yarjalu rajalan*" when a person lacks a mount and walks on his feet. So he is *rajil*, *rajil*, and *rajul* (with a *damma* on the *jim*), which is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. They say, "So-and-so walked barefoot, *rajulan*, to the House of God," as al-Tabari and others have related. The forms also include *rajlan*, *rajil*, and *rajl*. The plural is *rijal*, *rajla*, *rujjal*, *rajjala*, *rujala*, *rujlan*, *rijla*, *rijala* (with a *fatha* on the *jim*), *arjila*, *aras*, and *arajil*. *Rajul*, used as a generic noun, also takes the plural *rijal*.

**The second issue:** When God commanded standing before Him in prayer in the state of *qunut* (devout submission, which is dignity, tranquility, and the stilling of the limbs), and this is the usual state of safety and calm, He mentioned the occasional state of fear, and made clear that this worship does not lapse for the servant in any state. He granted His servants leave to pray on foot, *rijalan*, or mounted on horses, camels, or the like, by signalling with the head, *ima'an* and *ishara*, in whichever direction one faces. This is the view of the scholars. This is the prayer of the lone worshipper whom fear for his own life has distressed, whether in the state of sword combat, or from a predatory beast pursuing him, or from an enemy chasing him, or a flood carrying him away. In sum, every matter from which one fears for his soul permits what this verse includes.

**The third issue:** Included in this concession, by the consensus of the scholars, is that a person may, wherever he faces, move and turn and act according to his judgment for the preservation of his soul.

**The fourth issue:** Scholars differ regarding the fear in which prayer on foot or mounted is permitted. Al-Shafi'i said: it is the enemy's assault upon them, so that they see each other, while the Muslims are not in a fortress, until weapons reach them by shooting, or until the enemy comes closer to them than striking and stabbing range; or until someone whose report is trusted comes and informs him that the enemy is near him and that they are advancing toward him. If neither of these two conditions holds, it is not permitted for him to perform the prayer of fear. If they pray the prayer of fear on the basis of such a report and then the enemy leaves, they do not repeat it. It was said that they repeat it, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa.

Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) said: the state in which it is permitted for one in fear to pray on foot or mounted, facing the *qibla* or not facing it, is the state of extreme fear. The situation in which the reports were transmitted is other than this, namely the prayer of fear with an imam and the division of the people, and its ruling is not in this verse. Its explanation will come in Surat al-Nisa' (vol. 5, p. 351), God willing.

Malik distinguished between fear of an enemy who fights and fear of a beast of prey or the like, such as an attacking camel, a flood, or anything whose usual nature is destruction. He recommended, for fear other than that of an enemy, repetition within the time if safety occurs. Most jurists of the major cities hold that the matter is the same.

**The fifth issue:** Abu Hanifa said: fighting invalidates the prayer. The hadith of Ibn 'Umar refutes him, and the apparent meaning of the verse is the strongest proof against him. This will come in al-Nisa', God willing. Al-Shafi'i said: since the Blessed and Exalted One granted leave to omit some conditions, this indicates that fighting during the prayer does not invalidate it, and God knows best.

**The sixth issue:** There is no reduction in the number of units (*raka'at*) in the prayer of fear compared with the traveller's prayer, according to Malik, al-Shafi'i, and a group of scholars. Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, Qatada, and others said: one prays one *raka* by gesture. Muslim related from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: God prescribed the prayer through the tongue of the Messenger of God ﷺ as four in residence, two in travel, and one in fear.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas alone related this, and he is not an authority in what he alone transmits. Prayer is best when one is cautious, and whoever prays two units in fear and in travel has come out of disagreement into certainty.

Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: one in fear of death, in sword combat or otherwise, prays one *raka*; if he cannot, he says the takbir twice. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: if he is able only to say one takbir, it suffices for him. Ibn al-Mundhir related this.

And God's words, ﴿And when you are secure, remember God as He taught you﴾: that is, return to what you were commanded, namely completing the pillars (*arkan*). Mujahid said: "*amintum*" means you have left the abode of travel for the abode of residence, and al-Tabari rejected this view. A group said: "*amintum*" means your fear that compelled you to this prayer has ceased.

**The seventh issue:** Scholars differed on this topic regarding the one in fear who builds upon his prayer once he is secure. Malik said: if he prayed one *raka* while secure and then feared, he mounts and builds upon it; likewise if he prayed mounted while in fear and then became secure, he dismounts and builds. This is one of al-Shafi'i's two opinions, and al-Muzani held it. Abu Hanifa said: if he began the prayer while secure and then feared, he begins anew and does not build; but if he prayed in fear and then became secure, he builds. Al-Shafi'i said: the one who dismounts builds, but the one who mounts does not build. Abu Yusuf said: there is no building in any of this at all.

**The eighth issue:** God's words, ﴿remember God﴾. It was said: its meaning is give thanks to Him for this favour in teaching you this prayer, by which the sufficiency is achieved, and no prayer among the prayers has escaped you, and this is what you did not know. So the *ka* in His words "*kama*" carries the sense of gratitude. You say: "Do to me as I did to you, such and such," as recompense and thanks. And *ma* in His words "*ma lam*" is the object of "*'allamakum*".

**The ninth issue:** Our scholars, may God have mercy upon them, said: the prayer is originally supplication, and the state of fear is more fitting for supplication. For this reason the prayer does not lapse because of fear.
